agency: Washington State Criminal Justice Training Commission
outcome_detail: $500,000 combined settlement paid by the City of Federal Way and the Washington State Criminal Justice Training Commission, reported May 2025.
criminal_detail: No criminal charges were reported. The Washington State Criminal Justice Training Commission pursued administrative decertification proceedings against Officer Richard Klein; his certification was suspended in December 2024 with a two-year probationary period and 64 hours of remedial training required.
incident_date_approx: August-November 2022 (Basic Law Enforcement Academy attendance in Burien, WA)
description: Snohomish County Sheriff's Deputy Kaitlyn Ricksecker filed suit in King County Superior Court on April 26, 2024 against the Washington State Criminal Justice Training Commission, the City of Federal Way, and Federal Way police Officer Richard Klein, who served as an academy trainer. The suit alleged that while Ricksecker was a cadet at the state's Basic Law Enforcement Academy in 2022, Klein gave her a sexually derogatory nickname, used her body to demonstrate searches in front of the class, and touched her inappropriately with a baton, and that the academy tolerated a culture of sexism and sexual harassment. The City of Federal Way disputed the allegations and said it supported Klein. In May 2025, Federal Way and the training commission agreed to pay a combined $500,000 to settle the lawsuit. The commission separately suspended Klein's peace officer certification in December 2024, imposing a two-year probation and remedial training.
notes: Outside strict police-department definition (state law-enforcement training commission; accused trainer was a Federal Way Police Department officer). Companion record rec-66b covers an earlier, separate October 2023 lawsuit by two other former cadets against the same academy involving a different trainer.
